method: Audit all 15 GitHub default-branch commits in the six-calendar-month window, both merged PR bodies, issue inventory, source diffs, public corrected-behavior claims and newly added automated assertions. Count independently described defect groups once, not PRs, commits, parameterized test variants or test cases. Keep documented fixes with no specific regression in the denominator. New capabilities and tests of previously unbroken new functionality are excluded.
scope_limit: This is an observed public-source fixed-defect ledger, not a claim to recover undocumented pre-commit editing history or an external bug tracker. Grouping is explicit and reviewable. Two documented runtime claims (shuffle and reducer window) are included conservatively although their exact historical failure was not reconstructed. Upstream vulnerability floors are grouped as one project configuration-policy repair; no exact count of repaired upstream CVEs is claimed.

bug_groups.fixed_behavior: Classification F1 depends on batch partition instead of accumulated confusion counts.
bug_groups.regression_proof: Real Iris sklearn reference; batches 1,7,150 agree. The replacement stateful metric is the covered remedy; no claim that arbitrary user-selected stateless batch F1 is an epoch metric.
bug_groups.identification_basis: source diff and documented corrected behavior

bug_groups.regression_proof: Real breast-cancer (n,1) probabilities match sklearn binary F1.

assessment: 16 of 25 observed fixed-defect groups have added automated regression assertions (64%). Product behavior alone:12 of 14 (85.71%). Nine groups receive no regression credit. This is a reviewable group count, not a fixed-CVE count or recovery of undocumented pre-commit editing.
verification_scope: Existing public-source assertions and published execution receipts inspected. No new acceptance or remote-provider execution is asserted.
